title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you
why_read: A clever, well-executed niche project that reframes Wikipedia around physical proximity, likely interesting for its technical filtering/geo approach as much as its novelty.
analysis: This is a tool that filters Wikipedia articles down to only those tied to locations within roughly a half-hour walk of the user. It likely involves geocoding Wikipedia's geographic metadata and building a simple proximity-based search or map interface. The appeal is in the idea rather than deep technical novelty, but implementing accurate geo-filtering over a huge dataset at usable speed is a real engineering problem. High HN engagement suggests it resonated broadly, though the core technique is fairly well understood (geospatial indexing).
